key_insight: VEX-EHR, an open-weight language model adapted to local EHR data, outperformed gradient-boosted trees and CEHR-BERT on three clinical prediction tasks.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support discharge, readmission and ICU acute kidney injury prediction, with label-efficiency gains on selected tasks.
method: Extended a 12-billion-parameter model’s vocabulary with 17,601 clinical and audit-log codes.
Continued pretraining on 4.7 billion tokens from 170,483 patients’ 2019–2024 records.
Fine-tuned separately for each prediction task and compared against two baselines.
evidence_signal: At one academic medical center, VEX-EHR achieved AUROCs of 0.917 for next-24-hour discharge, 0.715 for 30-day readmission and 0.847 for ICU acute kidney injury; continued pretraining added 0.031–0.053 AUROC across tasks.
watch_item: Single-center results require external validation before assuming generalizability or clinical benefit.
paper_title: Continually pretrained open-weight language models can outperform traditional machine learning in EHR-based clinical prediction
